# Healthcare Informatics

Selected work from MBA 673 — Healthcare Information Systems, focused on using clinical data, SQL, R, visualization, and healthcare information systems to support better decisions.

## Analysis Reports

### Analysis Report One: What's Your Data Strategy?

An analysis of defensive and offensive data strategy in healthcare, using nutrition-related clinical data to examine early risk identification, data quality, and transitions of care.

[Read the publication →](analysis-report-01/index.qmd)

### Analysis Report Two: Data, Data Everywhere

An analysis of how connected clinical data can move healthcare from information collection to action, using nutrition support, laboratory, and ICU data to examine interoperability, clinical decision support, and earlier risk identification.

[Read the publication →](analysis-report-02/index.qmd)

### Analysis Report Three: Information Systems and Healthcare Provider Interactions

An analysis of how EHR design, documentation standards, workflow fit, and data quality affect provider interactions with healthcare information systems, using ICU weight and dietitian documentation to examine usability, trust, and readiness for advanced analytics.

[Read the publication →](analysis-report-03/index.qmd)

### Analysis Report Four: Health Privacy and Data Profiling

An analysis of health privacy, cybersecurity, and data profiling using a longitudinal MIMIC-III patient record to examine the value and sensitivity of connected EHR data, organizational resilience, and responsible data governance.

[Read the publication →](analysis-report-04/index.qmd)

### Analysis Report Five: Financial Modeling Using the MIMIC-III Database

A financial model combining MIMIC-III enteral nutrition utilization, estimated acquisition costs, and published clinical evidence to evaluate the potential clinical and financial value of an early peptide-based enteral nutrition protocol.

[Read the publication →](analysis-report-05/index.qmd)
